question: the RELATIONAL gain is +0.009 on 233 subjects with P=0.82-0.94 -- too weak to claim. Can power be improved without more subjects?
how: the cohort cannot be enlarged (972 = 753 + 263 with overlap). But a single 728->233 prediction includes the choice of training set. Repeat 20 times with a different random 90% of the training set each time (holdout always disjoint), average, bootstrap over the repeats.
verdict: THE GAIN IS NOW SEPARATED FROM ZERO. +0.0084 with 95% CI [0.0072, 0.0096] and every one of the 20 repeats positive. The single-split P of 0.82 was low power, not the absence of an effect: averaging over training-set choices removes the variance that dominated the single test.
why_averaging_over_training_sets_is_vali: every repeat still trains on subjects disjoint from the 233 holdout, so the holdout is never seen. The repeats differ only in WHICH training subjects are used, which is a nuisance parameter -- averaging over it is the standard way to reduce variance without touching the test set.
what_is_still_true_from_yesterday: the single fixed training set (all 728) gives +0.0086 at P=0.82, and the six-with-relational arm gives +0.0099 at P=0.94. Those are the numbers for one realisation; this is the number for the ensemble of realisations. Both belong in the record, and the latter is the one to quote for the effect size.
caveat_that_remains: the 0.001 CI half-width reflects only training-set variance. It does not include family structure (random 90% subsets ignore it) or cohort selection. So the effect is robust to training-set choice, not proven for every possible cohort.

CORRECTION_2026_11_18.what_was_wrong: the 95% CI [0.0072, 0.0096] and P=1.000 held the 233 holdout subjects FIXED across all 20 repeats. It measured training-set variance only -- the same 233 people every time -- so it is a pseudo-replicate and does not speak to generalisation to new subjects. Raised by the parallel session and correct.
CORRECTION_2026_11_18.the_valid_test: bag the 20 predictions per subject, then bootstrap over the 233 SUBJECTS (which is where the real uncertainty lives).
CORRECTION_2026_11_18.corrected_statement: RELATIONAL adds about +0.011 to the holdout prediction (bagged), 95% CI [-0.006, +0.029], P = 0.88. POSITIVE BUT NOT CONFIRMED. The earlier 'P=1.000, power problem solved' claim is withdrawn -- the point estimate barely moved (+0.0084 -> +0.0109), only the (wrong) interval did.
CORRECTION_2026_11_18.the_lesson: repeating over training sets cannot reduce holdout sampling noise by construction. Only more or different TEST subjects can do that, and this cohort has no more.
